title: Prompt Quest
blurb: Spells only work if your instructions are clear. Learn to talk to an AI so it does exactly what you want.
objectives: Why clear instructions get better AI results
How to add a target, constraints, and a role

glossary.def: The instructions you give an AI — your 'spell'.
A limit you add, like 'avoid allies' or 'keep it short'.
Who you ask the AI to act as, like 'a kind science teacher'.
The skill of writing clear instructions so an AI gives you what you actually want.

steps.title: Welcome to Wizard Academy
steps.body:
Spells here are powered by **prompts** — instructions for the AI wizard. And the wizard is very literal: it does *exactly* what you say, not what you *meant*.

Say “Attack!” and it might blast your own teammate. The fix isn't a better wizard — it's a **clearer spell**.

steps.title: Which spell works?
steps.prompt: Which instruction will the wizard follow more reliably?
choices: "Attack the nearest enemy with fire, and avoid allies."
steps.afterPick: The detailed one, every time. Vague leaves the AI guessing; specific leaves no room for mistakes. Let's prove it. →

steps.title: Build your spells
steps.youWillDo: build a clear spell from the parts and cast it
steps.body: Pick the **parts** that make each spell clear — the action, the target, the limits, and (later) a role. Skip the nonsense. Watch the **clarity meter**, then **Cast** and see what happens.

steps.title: What made spells work
steps.body:
The winning spells all had the same things:

- a clear **action** (what to do)
- a specific **target** (to whom/what)
- **constraints** (what to avoid)
- sometimes a **role** (“act as a teacher”)

Vague spells left gaps, and the AI filled them however it liked — usually wrong.

steps.title: Why be specific?
steps.question: Why does “Summon a friendly blue dragon that protects the villagers” beat “Summon a dragon”?
choices: It removes the AI's guesswork by saying exactly what you want
steps.explain: Clear details = fewer guesses = the result you actually wanted. That's the whole game of prompting.

steps.title: Say it your way
steps.prompt: What's one tip you'd give a friend for writing a prompt that gets good results?

recall.question: The best way to get what you want from an AI is to…
choices: Be clear and specific about what you want
Use as many big words as possible
recall.explain: Clear and specific wins. Say the goal, the limits, and the role.

steps.title: You're a prompt engineer now 🎉
steps.body:
This is exactly how people get great results from real AI tools like chatbots: **clear instructions, constraints, and a role**.

It even has a job title — *prompt engineering*. **Next up:** make sure the AI is fair to everyone, not just the group it saw most.
